Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Aurora Health)

Hi Sabrina / Jack,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — appreciate the candid walk-through of your inference workload and priorities. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Peak inference latency spikes under batch jobs during claims processing windows (10–12pm ET) causing SLA misses to downstream services.
- Cost volatility when using bursty on-demand capacity; desire for predictable monthly unit economics.
- Data isolation and compliance requirements for PHI (need VPC + customer-managed KMS).

Goals you mentioned:
- Stable 99th percentile latency < 250ms for RT scoring endpoints.
- Reserved GPU pool to cover baseline throughput (approx 300 qps sustained, peaks to 1k qps for 20–30 minutes).
- Audit logs and 12-month retention for access and inference events.

Proposed Dedicated capacity plan (initial):
- Reserved pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) with autoscale headroom to +4 GPUs for short peaks.
- Isolation: VPC peering + customer KMS integration; we will provide SOC2 artifacts and network diagrams.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool; per-route P99 targets configurable (we'll target P99 < 250ms as requested).
- Cost: preliminary monthly commit estimate in attached proposal (TBD after sizing call).

Next steps / asks:
1) Sizing call: propose Thu Jul 30 9:00–10:00am ET to review production traffic patterns and finalize GPU count. Can Marissa and I come on that?
2) Security checklist: Sabrina, please share your compliance checklist and any specific evidence types you need (e.g., KMS audit, SOC2 report).
3) Procurement timeline: Jack, any procurement lead times or PO cadence we should be aware of?

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-aurora.pdf — initial config + assumptions.

If the timing above works, we'll send a calendar invite. Thanks again — excited to help stabilize latency and bring cost predictability.

Best,
Ben Carter
